questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A uniform potentiometer wire of length 100 cm has a resistance of 10 Ω. It is connected in series with a resistance R and a battery of EMF 2 V having negligible internal resistance. If a balance length of 40 cm is obtained for an unknown EMF source of 10 mV, the value of the series resistance R is:
questions.officialExplanation: Potential gradient k = E_unknown / L_balance = 10 mV / 40 cm = (10 × 10⁻³ V) / 0.4 m = 0.025 V/m. Total potential drop across 1 m wire: V_wire = k × 1.0 m = 0.025 V. By voltage divider: V_wire = E_driver × R_wire / (R + R_wire) => 0.025 = 2 × 10 / (R + 10) => 0.025 (R + 10) = 20 => R + 10 = 20 / 0.025 = 800 => R = 790 Ω.
questions.speedHack: Wire drop is 25 mV for 100 cm. For 2 V battery, series resistance must take (2 - 0.025) V ≈ 1.975 V. (1.975 / 0.025) × 10 Ω = 79 × 10 = 790 Ω.
questions.commonTrap: Confusing balancing length with total wire length when computing gradient.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics, Chapter 3: Current Electricity, Potentiometer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A biconvex lens of focal length f_air = 20 cm in air made of glass of refractive index μ_g = 1.5 is immersed completely in a liquid of refractive index μ_l = 1.25. The new focal length of the lens in the liquid is:
questions.commonTrap: Using (μ_liquid - 1) instead of (μ_glass / μ_liquid - 1).
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics, Chapter 9: Ray Optics.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle of mass m moves in a circular orbit under the action of a central attractive force F = -k / r. The kinetic energy K and total mechanical energy E of the particle are related as:
questions.officialExplanation: Centripetal force: m v² / r = k / r => m v² = k. Kinetic energy K = (1/2) m v² = k / 2. Potential energy U: dU/dr = -F = k / r => U = k ln(r). For force law F ∝ rⁿ, virial theorem states 2K = n U. Here n = -1, but taking standard zero potential at r = 1, in a strictly bound orbit with 1/r force: when F = -k/r, 2K = -(-k) = k.
questions.speedHack: For 1/r force, speed v = √(k/m) is constant independent of radius.
questions.commonTrap: Confusing inverse-distance force F ∝ 1/r with inverse-square gravity F ∝ 1/r².
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Chapter 6: Work, Energy and Power.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The ratio of the radius of the 3rd orbit to the 2nd orbit of hydrogen atom according to Bohr model is:
questions.officialExplanation: According to Bohr's postulate, orbit radius r_n ∝ n² / Z. For hydrogen Z = 1, so r₃ / r₂ = 3² / 2² = 9 / 4.
questions.speedHack: Radius scales as square of principal quantum number n² => 3² / 2² = 9/4.
questions.commonTrap: Thinking radius scales linearly with n (confusing radius with de Broglie wavelength).
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics, Chapter 12: Atoms.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A long solenoid of radius 1 mm has 100 turns per mm. If 1 A current flows in the solenoid, the magnetic field strength at the centre of the solenoid is:
questions.officialExplanation: Turns per metre n = 100 turns / (10⁻³ m) = 10⁵ turns/m. B = μ₀ n I = (4π × 10⁻⁷) × 10⁵ × 1 = 4π × 10⁻² T = 4 × 3.1416 × 10⁻² T ≈ 12.56 × 10⁻² T.
conceptFormulae: n = N / L (turns per unit metre)
questions.commonTrap: Using n = 100 without converting mm to metres.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Physics, Chapter 4: Moving Charges.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following coordination complexes is diamagnetic and exhibits d²sp³ inner-orbital hybridization?
questions.officialExplanation: In [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺, cobalt is in +3 oxidation state (3d⁶). NH₃ is a strong field ligand according to the spectrochemical series and causes pairing of electrons in 3d orbitals (t₂g⁶ eg⁰). The two vacant 3d orbitals along with 4s and three 4p orbitals undergo d²sp³ hybridization, forming a low-spin, diamagnetic octahedral complex.
conceptFormulae: Strong field ligand forces pairing: t₂g⁶ eg⁰ => μ_spin = 0
questions.speedHack: Co³⁺ with strong field ligands (NH₃, CN⁻, en) is always low-spin diamagnetic d²sp³.
questions.commonTrap: Confusing with [CoF₆]³⁻ where F⁻ is a weak field ligand leading to sp³d² outer-orbital paramagnetic complex.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Chapter 9: Coordination Compounds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When benzaldehyde is heated with concentrated NaOH solution, it undergoes disproportionation to give benzoic acid and benzyl alcohol. This reaction is known as:
questions.officialExplanation: Aldehydes lacking α-hydrogen atoms (such as benzaldehyde C₆H₅CHO and formaldehyde HCHO) undergo self-oxidation and reduction (disproportionation) in presence of concentrated alkali (50% NaOH/KOH) to form one molecule of alcohol and one molecule of carboxylic acid salt. This is the classic Cannizzaro reaction.
questions.speedHack: Aldehyde with NO α-hydrogen + conc. NaOH = Cannizzaro in 5 seconds.
questions.commonTrap: Confusing with Aldol condensation which requires at least one α-hydrogen.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Chapter 12: Aldehydes and Ketones.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: For an isolated thermodynamic system undergoing a spontaneous process, which of the following criteria is ALWAYS true?
questions.officialExplanation: For an isolated system, there is no exchange of energy or matter with surroundings (q = 0, w = 0 => ΔU = 0 by First Law). By the Second Law of Thermodynamics, any spontaneous change in an isolated system leads to an increase in its entropy, hence ΔS_system > 0.
questions.speedHack: Isolated universe always tends toward maximum entropy (ΔS > 0) with conserved total energy (ΔU = 0).
questions.commonTrap: Applying ΔG < 0 which is defined at constant temperature and pressure, not for an isolated system.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Chapter 6: Thermodynamics.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion (VSEPR) theory, the geometry and shape of ClF₃ molecule are respectively:

options.label: B
options.text: Trigonal planar geometry and Trigonal planar shape

options.label: C
options.text: Octahedral geometry and Square planar shape

questions.officialExplanation: Chlorine has 7 valence electrons. In ClF₃, it forms 3 single bonds with fluorine atoms and retains 2 lone pairs. Steric number = 3 bond pairs + 2 lone pairs = 5, which corresponds to sp³d hybridization and trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry. To minimize lone pair-lone pair repulsions (Bent's rule), both lone pairs occupy equatorial positions, resulting in a T-shaped molecular geometry.
conceptFormulae: Steric Number = Bond pairs + Lone pairs = 3 + 2 = 5 (sp³d)
questions.speedHack: 7 - 3 = 4 electrons = 2 lone pairs. Steric 5 with 2 lone pairs is always T-shaped.
questions.commonTrap: Placing lone pairs in axial positions resulting in trigonal planar.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Chapter 4: Chemical Bonding.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: During DNA replication in prokaryotes, which enzyme is responsible for removing RNA primers and replacing them with deoxyribonucleotides, utilizing its 5' to 3' exonuclease activity?
questions.officialExplanation: DNA Polymerase I possesses unique 5' to 3' exonuclease activity (in addition to 5' to 3' polymerase and 3' to 5' proofreading exonuclease activities). It removes RNA primers ahead of the growing DNA chain and fills the gap with complimentary dNTPs during lagging strand synthesis.
conceptFormulae: DNA Pol I: 5'→3' exonuclease removes primers
DNA Pol III: primary replicative enzyme with 3'→5' proofreading
questions.speedHack: Only DNA Pol I has 5'→3' exonuclease activity for primer removal in E. coli.
questions.commonTrap: Selecting DNA Pol III which is the main elongating enzyme but lacks 5'→3' exonuclease.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 6: Molecular Basis of Inheritance.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In C4 plants, the primary carbon dioxide acceptor is a 3-carbon molecule called phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP). The primary CO₂ fixation enzyme PEP carboxylase is exclusively localized in the cytosol of which cell type?
questions.officialExplanation: In C4 plants (Kranz anatomy), mesophyll cells lack RuBisCO but possess high levels of PEP carboxylase in their cytoplasm. PEP carboxylase fixes atmospheric CO₂ (as HCO₃⁻) onto PEP to form 4-carbon oxaloacetate (OAA). Bundle sheath cells contain RuBisCO and lack PEPcase.
conceptFormulae: Bundle Sheath: Malate decarboxylation → Pyruvate + CO₂ → Calvin Cycle (RuBisCO)
questions.speedHack: Mesophyll = PEPcase (primary fixation); Bundle Sheath = RuBisCO (Calvin cycle).
questions.commonTrap: Thinking PEPcase is in bundle sheath cells.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 13: Photosynthesis in Higher Plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Recombination between homologous chromosomes is mediated by the enzyme recombinase and occurs during which specific substage of Prophase I in meiosis?
questions.officialExplanation: During Pachytene stage of Meiosis I, crossing over (recombination) occurs between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes at recombination nodules, mediated by enzyme recombinase. Zygotene features synapsis and synaptonemal complex; Diplotene features chiasmata dissolution.
questions.speedHack: Pachytene = Packing & Packaging DNA crossover (recombination).
questions.commonTrap: Confusing crossing over (Pachytene) with formation of synapsis (Zygotene).
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 10: Cell Cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In angiosperms, the functional megaspore undergoes three successive free-nuclear mitotic divisions to produce an 8-nucleate, 7-celled mature female gametophyte (embryo sac). At maturity, the egg apparatus consists of:

options.label: A
options.text: One egg cell and two synergids

options.label: B
options.text: Two egg cells and one synergid

options.label: D
options.text: One central cell with two polar nuclei

questions.officialExplanation: In a typical Polygonum-type embryo sac, three cells are grouped together at the micropylar end to constitute the egg apparatus. This consists of two synergids (bearing filiform apparatus to guide pollen tube entry) and one female gamete (egg cell).
conceptFormulae: Egg Apparatus = 1 Egg Cell + 2 Synergids (Micropylar end)
Central Cell = 1 cell with 2 Polar Nuclei
questions.speedHack: Micropylar pole = 2 helpers (synergids) + 1 queen (egg).
questions.commonTrap: Thinking antipodal cells form part of the egg apparatus.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 2: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following peptide hormones acts predominantly on the hepatocytes and adipocytes, stimulating glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, thereby leading to hyperglycemia?
questions.officialExplanation: Glucagon is a peptide hormone secreted by α-cells of the Islets of Langerhans. It maintains normal blood glucose levels by stimulating glycogenolysis (glycogen breakdown) in liver hepatocytes and promoting gluconeogenesis, thus acting as a hyperglycemic hormone. Insulin acts in opposition by promoting glycogenesis.
conceptFormulae: Insulin (β-cells): Glucose uptake + Glycogenesis → ↓ Blood Glucose (Hypoglycemic)
questions.speedHack: Glucagon = Glucose-is-GONE from cell into blood => Hyperglycemic.
questions.commonTrap: Confusing glucagon with insulin.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 22: Chemical Coordination.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: In the human cardiac cycle, the second heart sound ('dub') is produced due to which of the following mechanical events?

options.label: A
options.text: Rapid closure of the semilunar valves at the onset of ventricular diastole

options.label: B
options.text: Closure of the bicuspid and tricuspid valves at the beginning of ventricular systole

options.label: C
options.text: Opening of the semilunar valves during rapid ventricular ejection

options.label: D
options.text: Rushing of blood through the atrioventricular orifices during atrial systole

questions.officialExplanation: First heart sound (LUB) is caused by closure of AV valves (tricuspid and bicuspid) at the beginning of ventricular systole. Second heart sound (DUB) is caused by the sudden closure of the aortic and pulmonary semilunar valves at the onset of ventricular diastole to prevent backflow of blood.
conceptFormulae: S1 (Lub): Closure of AV valves (Ventricular Systole starts)
S2 (Dub): Closure of Semilunar valves (Ventricular Diastole starts)
questions.speedHack: LUB = AV close (Long, low pitch); DUB = Semilunar close (Short, high pitch).
questions.commonTrap: Believing heart sounds are produced by opening of valves rather than their snapping closure.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 18: Body Fluids and Circulation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which hormone surge triggers ovulation (rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of secondary oocyte) during the middle of a 28-day human menstrual cycle?
questions.officialExplanation: Both LH and FSH attain peak levels around day 14 of a 28-day menstrual cycle. Rapid secretion of LH leading to its maximum level mid-cycle, known as the 'LH surge', induces rupture of the mature Graafian follicle and thereby releases the secondary oocyte (ovulation).
conceptFormulae: LH Surge (Day 14) → Graafian Follicle Ruptures → Ovulation → Corpus Luteum
questions.speedHack: LH = Leaps Hormone (ruptures follicle into corpus luteum).
questions.commonTrap: Selecting progesterone, which only peaks in the luteal phase AFTER ovulation.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 3: Human Reproduction.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The forelimbs of humans, cheetahs, whales, and bats possess identical fundamental anatomical bone structures (humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals) but perform different physiological functions. This anatomical pattern illustrates:

options.label: A
options.text: Homologous organs arising from divergent evolution

options.label: B
options.text: Analogous organs arising from convergent evolution

options.label: D
options.text: Vestigial adaptations due to Lamarckian inheritance

questions.officialExplanation: Homologous organs share common anatomical origin and basic structure, developed along different directions due to adaptations to different needs (divergent evolution). Vertebrate forelimbs share the same skeletal elements despite serving running, swimming, or flying.
conceptFormulae: Homology: Same Origin, Different Function → Divergent Evolution
Analogy: Different Origin, Same Function → Convergent Evolution
questions.speedHack: Home (same ancestor) = Homologous = Divergent.
questions.commonTrap: Confusing with analogous structures like wings of butterfly and wings of bird.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 7: Evolution.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The escape velocity from the Earth's surface is v_e = 11.2 km/s. If a body is projected from the surface with speed v = 3 v_e, its speed in interplanetary space far away from the Earth's gravitational influence will be:
questions.officialExplanation: By conservation of mechanical energy between Earth's surface and infinity: (1/2) m v² - (1/2) m v_e² = (1/2) m v_∞² => v_∞ = √(v² - v_e²). Here v = 3 v_e, so v_∞ = √((3v_e)² - v_e²) = √(9 - 1) v_e = √8 v_e = 2√2 v_e.
conceptFormulae: 1/2 m v² - G M m / R = 1/2 m v_∞²
questions.speedHack: v_inf = √(3² - 1) v_e = √8 v_e = 2√2 v_e in 5 seconds.
questions.commonTrap: Simply subtracting velocities (3v_e - v_e = 2v_e) instead of subtracting energies.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Chapter 8: Gravitation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The molar conductivity of a 0.001 M acetic acid solution is 48.15 S cm² mol⁻¹. If limiting molar conductivity at infinite dilution Λ°_m is 390.5 S cm² mol⁻¹, the degree of dissociation α of acetic acid is approximately:
questions.officialExplanation: According to Kohlrausch's law and Arrhenius theory, degree of dissociation α = Λ_m / Λ°_m = 48.15 / 390.5 ≈ 0.1233 or 12.33%.
questions.commonTrap: Multiplying by concentration instead of straightforward ratio.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Chemistry, Chapter 3: Electrochemistry.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Which of the following ecological pyramids is ALWAYS upright and can never be inverted in any ecosystem?

options.label: B
options.text: Pyramid of biomass in an aquatic ecosystem

options.label: C
options.text: Pyramid of numbers in a parasitic tree ecosystem

options.label: D
options.text: Pyramid of biomass in a forest ecosystem

questions.officialExplanation: The pyramid of energy is always upright because when energy flows from a particular trophic level to the next trophic level, some energy is always lost as heat at each step (Lindeman's 10% law). Therefore, energy available at higher trophic levels is strictly less than that at lower levels.
conceptFormulae: Second Law of Thermodynamics in Ecosystems
questions.speedHack: Energy ALWAYS decreases upwards due to heat dissipation. Never inverted.
questions.commonTrap: Confusing with pyramid of biomass in sea, which is inverted (zooplankton > phytoplankton).
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 14: Ecosystem.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Under normal resting physiological conditions in a healthy human, every 100 mL of oxygenated blood delivers approximately how much oxygen to the tissues?
questions.officialExplanation: Under normal resting physiological conditions, 100 mL of oxygenated blood contains about 20 mL of O₂. Of this, about 5 mL of O₂ is delivered to the tissues, and 15 mL remains bound to hemoglobin in deoxygenated blood returning to the heart. (Note: 100 mL deoxygenated blood delivers ~4 mL of CO₂ to alveoli).
conceptFormulae: 100 mL oxygenated blood carries ~20 mL O₂
Resting tissue delivery = 5 mL O₂ / 100 mL blood
CO₂ delivery to alveoli = 4 mL CO₂ / 100 mL blood
questions.speedHack: O₂ delivered = 5 mL. CO₂ delivered = 4 mL. Clear NCERT direct lines.
questions.commonTrap: Confusing total oxygen content (20 mL) with oxygen delivered to tissues (5 mL), or confusing with CO₂ (4 mL).
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Chapter 17: Breathing and Exchange of Gases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A physical quantity P is related to four observables a, b, c and d as follows: P = (a³ b²) / (√c d). The percentage errors of measurement in a, b, c and d are 1%, 3%, 4% and 2% respectively. What is the percentage error in the quantity P?
questions.speedHack: Multiply powers by percentage errors: 3(1) + 2(3) + 0.5(4) + 1(2) = 3 + 6 + 2 + 2 = 13%.
questions.commonTrap: Subtracting the denominator power error instead of adding it.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Units and Measurements.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upwards with a velocity u. It passes three points A, B, and C at heights h, 2h, and 3h with velocities v_A, v_B, and v_C respectively. The ratio of (v_A² - v_B²) to (v_B² - v_C²) is:
questions.officialExplanation: By third equation of motion: v² = u² - 2gh. Thus v_A² = u² - 2gh, v_B² = u² - 4gh, v_C² = u² - 6gh. v_A² - v_B² = 2gh, and v_B² - v_C² = 2gh. The ratio is 2gh / 2gh = 1 : 1.
questions.speedHack: v² drops by equal amounts (2gΔh) across equal height increments Δh = h.
questions.commonTrap: Using v instead of v² and getting a radical ratio.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Straight Line.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If the magnitude of the sum of two vectors A and B is equal to the magnitude of their difference, i.e., |A + B| = |A - B|, the angle θ between vector A and vector B is:
questions.officialExplanation: |A + B|² = A² + B² + 2 A B cos θ. |A - B|² = A² + B² - 2 A B cos θ. Equating gives 4 A B cos θ = 0 => cos θ = 0 => θ = 90°.
questions.speedHack: Diagonals of a parallelogram are equal if and only if it is a rectangle (perpendicular vectors).
questions.commonTrap: Assuming vectors must be equal in magnitude.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Motion in a Plane & Vectors.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A block of mass 10 kg is placed on a rough horizontal surface having coefficient of static friction μ_s = 0.5 and kinetic friction μ_k = 0.4. If a horizontal force of 40 N is applied on the block, the frictional force acting on the block is (Take g = 10 m/s²):
questions.officialExplanation: Maximum limiting static friction f_lim = μ_s N = 0.5 × (10 × 10) = 50 N. Since applied force F = 40 N < f_lim, the block remains stationary. For a stationary block, static friction is self-adjusting and equals applied force: f = 40 N.
conceptFormulae: Self-adjusting friction when body doesn't slide
questions.speedHack: Applied force (40 N) < Limiting friction (50 N) => Friction exactly opposes applied force = 40 N.
questions.commonTrap: Automatically multiplying μ_k N or μ_s N and choosing 50 N.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Laws of Motion & Friction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A solid cylinder of mass M and radius R rolls without slipping down an inclined plane of angle θ. The linear acceleration a of the center of mass of the cylinder is:
questions.officialExplanation: For pure rolling on incline: a = g sin θ / (1 + I/(MR²)). For solid cylinder, I = (1/2) MR², so a = g sin θ / (1 + 1/2) = (2/3) g sin θ.
questions.speedHack: Acceleration = g sin θ / (1 + β). For cylinder β = 1/2 => a = (2/3) g sin θ.
questions.commonTrap: Using hollow cylinder formula (1/2 g sin θ).
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics, System of Particles & Rotational Motion.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A Carnot engine having an efficiency of η = 1/10 is used as a refrigerator. If work of 10 J is done on the refrigerator working between the same reservoirs, the amount of heat absorbed from the cold reservoir is:
questions.officialExplanation: Coefficient of performance β = (1 - η) / η = (1 - 1/10) / (1/10) = (9/10) / (1/10) = 9. Since β = Q_cold / W, Q_cold = β × W = 9 × 10 J = 90 J.
questions.speedHack: β = (1 - η) / η = 9. Heat absorbed = 9 × 10 = 90 J directly.
questions.commonTrap: Using Q = W / η = 100 J which is heat rejected to the hot reservoir.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Physics, Thermodynamics.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the mass of precipitate formed when 50 mL of 16.9% solution of AgNO₃ is mixed with 50 mL of 5.8% NaCl solution? (Ag = 108, N = 14, O = 16, Na = 23, Cl = 35.5):
questions.officialExplanation: Mass of AgNO₃ = 50 × (16.9 / 100) = 8.45 g. Molar mass of AgNO₃ = 170 g/mol => Moles of AgNO₃ = 8.45 / 170 = 0.0497 ≈ 0.05 mol. Mass of NaCl = 50 × (5.8 / 100) = 2.9 g. Molar mass of NaCl = 58.5 g/mol => Moles of NaCl = 2.9 / 58.5 = 0.0496 ≈ 0.05 mol. Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ → AgCl(s). 0.05 moles of AgCl formed. Mass of AgCl = 0.05 × 143.5 g/mol = 7.175 g ≈ 7.16 g.
questions.speedHack: Both reagents are in 1:1 stoichiometric ratio (~0.05 mol). Mass = 0.05 × 143.5 ≈ 7.17 g.
questions.commonTrap: Calculating for total volume of 100 mL without accounting for percentage composition.
questions.ncertRef: NCERT Class 11 Chemistry, Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry.

questions.question: The solubility product K_sp of CaF₂ at 298 K is 3.2 × 10⁻¹¹. The solubility of CaF₂ in a 0.1 M NaF aqueous solution is:

questions.question: In a Wheatstone bridge circuit for NEET 2026, four resistances P = 10 Ω, Q = 20 Ω, R = 15 Ω and S = 30 Ω are connected in cyclic order. A galvanometer of resistance 50 Ω is connected across the bridge. The equivalent resistance between the battery terminals is:

Equivalent resistance = (P + Q) || (R + S) = (30 × 45) / (30 + 45) = 1350 / 75 = 18 Ω. If connected between opposite pairs, R_eq = (10+15)||(20+30) = 25 × 50 / 75 = 50/3 ≈ 16.67 Ω.

questions.question: For the reaction 2A + B → Products, when concentration of A is doubled keeping [B] constant, the rate of reaction increases four-fold. When concentration of B is doubled keeping [A] constant, the rate is doubled. The overall order of the reaction in NEET 2026 is:
